## 2. Matrix instructions {#matrix}

For the [default wave32 dense WMMA configuration](#default-wmma-configuration), RDNA 4 halves the per-lane A/B fragment size while retaining eight FP32 C/D values per lane. Check the operand interface first, then register overlap and memory readiness; the sections below keep these separate requirements explicit.

:::: {.note}

**RDNA 4 sparse matrix semantics:** SWMMAC uses 2:4 sparse A, dense B, and position metadata. For FP16 16×16×32, logical K=32 and stored A has K=16. [ISA p.100](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=100 "ISA instruction table") · [ISA p.106](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=106 "ISA sparse dimensions").

### WMMA spacing and operand readiness {#wmma-waits}

:::: {.note}

The rules here describe the ISA contract. The [LLVM handling reference](../rdna-llvm-dependencies/index.qmd#llvm-wmma-handling) separately identifies automatic compiler actions, their conditions, and their limits at a fixed source revision.

::::

**Register dependency:** D → A/B and D → C refer to the preceding instruction’s destination and the following instruction’s sources, not to equality of matrix values. If D overlaps both C and A/B, the D → A/B correctness rule still applies; RDNA 4 also includes the sparse index input. Absence of an explicit D → C gap does not imply zero latency or stall-free execution. [RDNA 3](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna3-shader-instruction-set-architecture-feb-2023.pdf#page=82) · [RDNA 3.5](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna35_instruction_set_architecture.pdf#page=86) · [RDNA 4](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=101).

**V\_NOP:** a vector no-op, not a memory-completion test. RDNA 4 explicitly defines it as a single-cycle bubble in the vector ALU pipeline. The WMMA overlap rule names `V_NOP` or an independent VALU instruction as the separator; a scalar `S_NOP` or scalar memory-counter wait is not one of those specified substitutes. [RDNA 3 V\_NOP](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna3-shader-instruction-set-architecture-feb-2023.pdf#page=274) · [RDNA 3.5 V\_NOP](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna35_instruction_set_architecture.pdf#page=292) · [RDNA 4 V\_NOP](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=315); the overlap-rule sources are in the table above.

**Memory-produced operands:** the input read has its own completion dependency. RDNA 3 / 3.5 `S_WAITCNT` and RDNA 4 `S_WAIT_*CNT` test outstanding-operation counters against thresholds. Use the producer-specific counter in the [completion-wait table](#memory-completion-waits); the [shared map](#dependency-wait-overview) explains why a WMMA separator cannot replace that wait. [RDNA 3 §§5.6–5.7, pp.52–53](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna3-shader-instruction-set-architecture-feb-2023.pdf#page=52) · [RDNA 3.5 §§5.6–5.7, pp.53–54](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna35_instruction_set_architecture.pdf#page=53) · [RDNA 4 §5.7, pp.61–65](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=61).

**S\_DELAY\_ALU:** the manuals separately describe this as optional ALU dependency scheduling that can avoid pipeline stalls; it is not required for correct operation. This statement does not remove the explicit WMMA overlap rule above. [RDNA 3 §5.7](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna3-shader-instruction-set-architecture-feb-2023.pdf#page=53) · [RDNA 3.5 §5.7](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna35_instruction_set_architecture.pdf#page=54) · [RDNA 4 §5.8](https://gpuopen.com/download/rdna4-instruction-set-architecture.pdf#page=66).
